overview.title: What is Próspera?
overview.text: Próspera is a special economic zone on Roatán island, Honduras, designed for entrepreneurs seeking streamlined governance and a 1% effective income tax. Businesses register online in under 24 hours, and registered residents from 40+ countries can own property, vote on governance matters, and participate in Próspera's digital governance platform.

overview.title: Who Joins Próspera?
overview.text: Próspera attracts biotech researchers, crypto founders, nearshoring operators, and investors drawn to its streamlined legal framework and competitive taxes. The zone counts 1,700+ registered residents (e-residents and on-site residents combined) from over 40 countries, 250+ incorporated businesses as of December 2024, and 950 active direct jobs. Backers include Brian Armstrong of Coinbase, Tim Draper, and Balaji Srinivasan.

overview.title: Próspera's Legal and Tax Framework
overview.text: As a Zone for Employment and Economic Development (ZEDE), Próspera operates under its own civil and commercial codes independent of Honduran national law. Businesses can choose applicable regulatory frameworks from approved foreign jurisdictions or propose custom rules. Bitcoin is recognized as legal tender, wages must be at least 25% above Honduras's national minimum, and a legal stability guarantee locks in your applicable tax rates for life.

history.text:
Próspera was conceived by Venezuelan entrepreneur Erick Brimen as a poverty-relief initiative using private-sector governance. Brimen secured a ZEDE charter in late 2017 after acquiring land on Roatán's north coast, attracting backing from venture firm Pronomos Capital - whose investors include Peter Thiel and Marc Andreessen - along with endorsements from Balaji Srinivasan and Tim Draper.

Construction of Duna Tower, the zone's first residential building, began in 2021. That same year, Próspera recognized Bitcoin as legal tender and expanded its footprint to over 1,000 incorporated acres. The ePróspera digital governance platform, built with Estonian e-government experts, launched to enable online business registration and residency applications.

In April 2022, Honduran President Xiomara Castro signed legislation repealing the ZEDE framework. Honduras Próspera Inc. filed a $10.7 billion damages claim with the International Centre for Settlement of Investment Disputes, citing CAFTA-DR investor protections. The zone has continued operating throughout the legal dispute, with Deloitte issuing a legal validation in December 2024 affirming operational continuity.

Duna Tower reached 100% occupancy for three consecutive months by March 2025. E-Residency applications resumed in December 2024 after a brief pause, and in January 2025 Coinbase and its venture arm announced an investment alongside North Island Ventures and BoostVC.

location:
Próspera's main campus sits on the north coast of Roatán, the largest of Honduras's Bay Islands, about 20 minutes by road from Juan Manuel Galvez International Airport. The zone divides into two districts: the Beta District (58 acres) anchored by [Duna Tower](https://wiki.prospera.city/Duna%20Tower), Roatán's tallest building and a mixed-use commercial and residential hub, and [Pristine Bay](https://pristinebay.com) (360 acres), a resort campus roughly 15-20 minutes' walk east featuring Las Verandas Hotel, the Black Pearl Golf Course, and [Pristine Academy](https://pristineacademy.co), a U.S.-accredited bilingual Montessori-inspired K-12 school that is part of the Próspera zone.

The total incorporated area covers more than 1,000 acres. Próspera is also developing a nearshoring manufacturing hub in La Ceiba on the Honduran mainland. Direct flights connect Roatán's airport to Miami, Houston, Dallas, Atlanta, and Toronto.
duration:
Próspera members set their own schedule based on residency tier. E-residents ($130/year) may spend up to 30 days per calendar year in the zone while retaining full business and property rights remotely. Full residents add continuous year-round access for the same base fee plus mandatory liability insurance.

For a first visit, a free Visitor Pass allows access for up to 30 nights. Monthly [Próspera Weekends](https://prospera.co/en) cost $450 per person, include housing and meals, and run 2-3 days. The 2026 calendar includes June 5-7, July 17-19, and August 28-30. Noma Family, a structured family coliving program, runs July 5 to August 2, 2026.
pricing:
Próspera offers four entry tiers:

Visitor Pass: Free. Up to 30 nights in the zone with limited work rights. No property ownership or business registration.

E-Residency: $130/year. Up to 30 days per calendar year in the zone. Includes full business registration rights, property ownership, and access to the ePróspera governance platform. Applications processed in 1-3 business days at portal.eprospera.com.

Full Residency: $130/year plus mandatory liability insurance. Continuous year-round physical access with all e-Residency benefits included.

Próspera Weekend: $450 per person, includes housing and food. Monthly 2-3 day visits for prospective members exploring the community. 2026 dates: June 5-7, July 17-19, August 28-30.

Business formation from $379 online, with entity recognition in under 24 hours.

howToEnter.text:
Apply online at [portal.eprospera.com](https://portal.eprospera.com). Choose your residency tier (Visitor Pass, e-Residency, or full Residency), submit a government-issued ID and proof of address, complete biometric identity verification, and sign the Agreement of Coexistence. Most applications are approved within 1-3 business days. Applicants from 18 restricted countries require an exemption before applying.

For those wanting to explore first, monthly [Próspera Weekends](https://prospera.co/en) cost $450 per person with housing and food included. A free weekly onboarding call runs Wednesdays at 7:00 PM UTC for prospective members with questions.

longtermer: Full Residency grants continuous year-round physical access to Próspera at $130/year plus mandatory liability insurance - the same base cost as e-Residency but without the 30-day cap. Long-term residents can lease units through [Duna Residences](https://www.dunaresidences.com), where Vitalia manages roughly 30 units on one-year lease terms with renewal options, or purchase property directly through Pristine Bay's real estate team.

kidFriendly.description: Próspera has dedicated family infrastructure. [Pristine Academy](https://pristineacademy.co), a U.S.-accredited bilingual Montessori-inspired K-12 school, operates in the Pristine Bay district roughly 15-20 minutes' walk from Duna Tower and is formally part of the Próspera zone. The Noma Family coliving program (July 5 to August 2, 2026) offers a structured extended stay designed for families with children.

faqs.question: What is Próspera and where is it located?
faqs.answer: Próspera is a special economic zone (ZEDE) on Roatán island, Honduras, founded by Erick Brimen and operational since 2020. It offers its own legal framework, a 1% effective income tax on gross revenue, and online business registration. The main campus is about 20 minutes from Roatán's international airport.

faqs.question: What is the difference between e-Residency and full Residency in Próspera?
faqs.answer: E-Residency ($130/year) grants 30 days of physical access per calendar year plus full business registration and property ownership rights. Full Residency adds year-round physical access for the same $130 base fee plus mandatory liability insurance. A free Visitor Pass allows access for up to 30 nights with limited work rights. [Apply at portal.eprospera.com](https://portal.eprospera.com/).

faqs.question: Is Próspera still operating after the Honduras Supreme Court ruling?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Honduran Supreme Court ruled ZEDEs unconstitutional in September 2024, but Próspera continues to operate under CAFTA-DR investor protections - a trade agreement that shields investors from retroactive legal changes. Deloitte issued a legal validation in December 2024 affirming operational continuity. Honduras Próspera Inc. has filed a $10.7 billion ICSID arbitration claim against the Honduran government.

faqs.question: How do I start a business in Próspera?
faqs.answer: Businesses register online at [portal.eprospera.com](https://portal.eprospera.com/) in under 24 hours, starting from $379. You select a regulatory framework from approved foreign jurisdictions or propose custom rules. The effective tax rate is 1% on gross business revenue. e-Residency ($130/year) is required for business registration.

faqs.question: What is a Próspera Weekend and how do I attend?
faqs.answer: [Próspera Weekends](https://prospera.co/en) are monthly 2-3 day visits to Roatán for $450 per person, with housing and food included. They include guided zone tours, networking with current residents and entrepreneurs, and time to explore the island. 2026 dates include June 5-7, July 17-19, and August 28-30. Book through the events section on prospera.co.

faqs.question: What healthcare is available in Próspera?
faqs.answer: Duna Tower houses three healthcare providers: Infinita Forever Health Clinic for primary and emergency care, GARM Clinic specializing in regenerative medicine and stem cell therapies, and a Clinica Cemesa branch with 24/7 emergency services. Próspera's regulatory flexibility has attracted biotech activity - Bryan Johnson received a gene therapy at Próspera that was not available in other jurisdictions, with Próspera citing research timelines accelerated by 70% versus comparable zones.

faqs.question: How many businesses and residents does Próspera have?
faqs.answer: Próspera surpassed 250 incorporated companies in December 2024 and has 950 active direct jobs and more than $100 million in catalyzed investment. The zone counts 1,700+ registered residents - combining both on-site physical residents and e-residents - from over 40 countries. Duna Tower, the primary residential building, reached 100% occupancy for three consecutive months by March 2025.

faqs.question: What is the tax rate in Próspera?
faqs.answer: Business revenue is taxed at an effective 1% rate (technically 10% applied to 10% of gross income). Personal income is taxed at 5%, wages at 5%, and sales at 2.5%. Wages within the zone must be at least 25% above Honduras's national minimum wage. Próspera's legal stability guarantee means your applicable tax rates and regulations cannot change without your individual consent.

faqs.question: Can families live in Próspera?
faqs.answer: Yes. [Pristine Academy](https://pristineacademy.co), a U.S.-accredited bilingual Montessori-inspired K-12 school, operates in the Pristine Bay district about 15-20 minutes' walk from Duna Tower. The Noma Family coliving program (July 5 to August 2, 2026) is specifically designed for families wanting an extended stay. Roatán's reef and tropical climate make it a practical year-round base.

faqs.question: What coworking and workspace does Próspera offer?
faqs.answer: Duna Tower's ground floor hosts Infinita Co-working Space with desk space, startup acceleration programming, and pitch events. The Beta Building, a 3-5 minute walk away, provides additional office space and conference rooms. A makerspace with 3D printing, hydroponics, and a community kitchen is also available. Internet via NetMan runs at 40-80 Mbps for $55-95/month.

faqs.question: How do I get to Próspera on Roatán?
faqs.answer: Roatán is served by Juan Manuel Galvez International Airport (RTB) with direct flights from Miami, Houston, Dallas, Atlanta, and Toronto via American Airlines, United, Delta, and Air Canada. From the airport, Próspera is about 15-20 minutes by taxi. A free weekly onboarding call runs Wednesdays at 7:00 PM UTC for those with questions before visiting.

faqs.question: Is Bitcoin accepted in Próspera?
faqs.answer: Yes - Bitcoin is recognized as legal tender within Próspera. A Bitcoin ATM operates in Duna Tower, and the Pristine Bay district has a dedicated Bitcoin Center. Brian Armstrong of Coinbase announced an investment in Próspera in January 2025, and Bitcoin Infinity Day is an annual event (August 21, 2026).
